title: Conversion Operators
description: Learn to convert between different collection types using LINQ conversion operators.

data.text: Conversion operators in LINQ convert the type of elements in a sequence (collection). There are three types:

items: **As operators** (AsEnumerable, AsQueryable) — Cast to IEnumerable<T> or IQueryable<T>
**To operators** (ToArray, ToList, ToDictionary, ToLookup) — Force execution and convert
**Casting operators** (Cast, OfType) — Convert non-generic to generic collections

data.text: The `AsEnumerable` and `AsQueryable` methods cast or convert a source object to `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>` respectively.

data.title: AsEnumerable & AsQueryable

data.text: The `Cast<T>()` method converts a non-generic collection to a generic collection.

data.title: Cast Example

data.text: The `To` operators force query execution and convert the result to a specific collection type.

Forcing Query Execution
data.text: To operators force immediate execution of deferred queries. This is important when working with remote data sources like databases.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cast converts non-generic to generic collections
To operators force query execution and convert types
ToArray, ToList, ToDictionary are commonly used
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn about generation operators.
